extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants / practitioners (RCE practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing, processing, and examiner treatment of Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114, including eligibility, required submissions, fees, and procedural consequences (after final, after allowance, after appeal, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for filing an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may obtain continued examination by filing a request for continued examination (RCE) (form PTO/SB/30), a submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: (A) payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 is granted); (B) abandonment of the application; or (C) the filing of a notice of appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or the commencement of a civil action (unless the appeal or civil action is terminated). The RCE provisions of 37 CFR 1.114 do not apply to: (A) a provisional application; (B) an application for a utility or plant patent filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before June 8, 1995; (C) an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before June 8, 1995; (D) an application for a design patent; or (E) a patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant cannot request continued examination until after prosecution is closed. Prosecution is closed if the application is under appeal, or the last Office action is a final action (37 CFR 1.113), a notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.311), or an action that otherwise closes prosecution (e.g., Ex parte Quayle). See 37 CFR 1.114(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' as used in 37 CFR 1.114 includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability. If a reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for suspension of action, an appeal brief or a reply brief (or related papers) will not be considered a submission under 37 CFR 1.114, but the submission may consist of arguments in a previously filed appeal brief or reply brief or incorporate them by reference. Previously filed after-final amendments (whether or not entered) may satisfy the submission requirement. See 37 CFR 1.114(c) and 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing verification checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel will verify that: (A) the RCE was filed on or after May 29, 2000; (B) the application was filed on or after June 8, 1995; (C) the application is a utility or plant application (not a design application); (D) the application was pending (not patented or abandoned) when the RCE was filed; (E) prosecution in the application is closed; (F) the RCE was filed before payment of the issue fee or, if not, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue was filed and granted; and (G) the RCE was accompanied by the proper fee(s) including the RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any condition is not satisfied, applicant will be notified (generally via Form PTO-2051). An improper RCE will not toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE have not been satisfied, the applicant will be notified and a 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE),' Form PTO-2051, will generally be mailed. An improper RCE will not operate to toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner discovers an improper RCE forwarded in error, the application should be returned to a head supervisory legal instruments examiner (HSLIE). If prosecution is not closed, applicant will be notified and any amendment/reply will be entered and forwarded to the examiner for consideration under 37 CFR 1.111. If the application is under appeal and the RCE lacked required fee/submission, it will be forwarded to the examiner for appropriate treatment and applicant notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal paper handling (CPA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper is ambiguous as to whether it is a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 (e.g., contains references to both), and the application is a plant or utility application filed on or after June 8, 1995, the Office will treat the transmittal paper as an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114. If ambiguous and the application is a design application, the Office will treat the transmittal paper as a request for a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other papers filed with the transmittal paper (e.g., preliminary amendment or IDS) are not considered in determining whether the transmittal paper is a CPA, an RCE, or ambiguous. An unambiguous transmittal paper that is an RCE in a design application will be treated as an improper RCE and Form PTO-2051 mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conditional RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and payment of the RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e) (i.e., an authorization to charge the fee to a deposit account in the event the submission would not otherwise be entered), the Office will treat the 'conditional' RCE and payment as if an RCE and payment of the fee had been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of proper RCE — entry of amendments and order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conditions for filing an RCE have been satisfied, the technical support personnel will process the proper RCE. Any previously filed unentered amendments and amendments filed with the RCE will normally be entered. Such amendments will be entered in the order in which they were filed in the absence of any specific instructions for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant files conflicting instructions about entry, applicant should clarify which amendments should be entered upon filing the RCE (and fee). Applicants are encouraged to file all amendments no later than the filing of the RCE to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). If additional time is needed to prepare a supplement, consider filing a suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(c) with the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for excess and new claims with RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant does not need to pay a fee for excess claims previously paid for prior to the filing of the RCE. New claims in excess of the number previously paid for, which are filed with the RCE or thereafter, will require payment of the appropriate fee(s) under 37 CFR 1.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE; conversion to new application limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 14, 2003, CPA practice under 37 CFR 1.53(d) does not apply to utility and plant applications. If an applicant files a request for a CPA of a utility or plant application filed on or after June 8, 1995, the Office will automatically treat the improper CPA as an RCE of the prior application under 37 CFR 1.114. If the CPA does not satisfy the requirements of 37 CFR 1.114 (e.g., lacks a submission or fee), the improper CPA will be treated as an improper RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not convert an improper CPA into an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) simply because requested. Conversion to 1.53(b) will occur only if applicant shows extenuating circumstances warranting the burdensome conversion process (e.g., application already issued as a patent and restoration to pending status and correction of improper RCE is not possible). Use Form paragraph 7.42.15 to inform applicant that a CPA is being treated as an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: After final rejection — withdrawal of finality and timely submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files an RCE with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) and a submission that meets the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action to which a reply is outstanding and the submission will be entered and considered. The submission must be timely received to continue prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the fee alone will not toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment. Any amendment that is an amendment must comply with the manner of making amendments set forth in 37 CFR 1.121 and include markings showing changes relative to the last entered amendment. Previously filed unentered after-final amendments may satisfy 1.114(c), but applicants are encouraged to file an amendment at the time of filing the RCE that incorporates desired changes and gives instructions regarding unentered amendments. Use Form paragraph 7.42.04 if RCE is proper after final rejection; use 7.42.08 if submission does not comply with 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submission — bona fide attempt requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive to the final Office action, then it must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply. If the submission is not a bona fide attempt, the RCE should be treated as an improper RCE and a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (Form PTO-2051) should be mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-bona fide submissions: an IDS only when a reply is outstanding; an amendment that cancels all claims without new or substitute claims. If the submission is a bona fide attempt but not fully responsive, applicant should be informed why and given a shortened statutory period of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) to complete the reply (use Form paragraph 7.42.08). Sub-situations: (A) Non-compliant amendment — treat as proper RCE, mail Notice of Noncompliant Amendment and give one month/30 days to provide compliant amendment (see 37 CFR 1.121 and MPEP § 714.03). (B) Presentation of claims for different invention — cannot switch inventions; treat as proper RCE but do not enter the amendment and give time to submit a complete reply (see 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 821.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) provides that 'No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.' Any amendment entered pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 that is determined to contain new matter should be treated in the same manner as a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 determined to contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant seeks to add new matter to the disclosure of an application, the procedure in 37 CFR 1.114 is not available and the applicant must file a continuation-in-part application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) containing such new matter. See MPEP § 706.03(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: First action final after filing an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: The action immediately subsequent to the filing of an RCE with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 may be made final only if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b) for making a first action final in a continuing application are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form paragraph 7.42.09 if appropriate to make the first action after filing the RCE final. When made final, shortened statutory periods and extension policies apply (e.g., shortened period of three months set to expire, with advisory-action timing rules; no statutory period will expire later than six months from mailing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: After allowance or Ex parte Quayle action — reopening prosecution and issue fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'withdraw the finality of any Office action' in 37 CFR 1.114(d) includes withdrawal of finality of a final rejection and the closing of prosecution by an Office action under Ex parte Quayle or notice of allowance. If an applicant files an RCE with the fee and a submission in an application that has been allowed, prosecution will be reopened provided the RCE is filed prior to payment of the issue fee (or, if issue fee paid, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw the application from issue is filed and granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issue fee has been paid, payment of the RCE fee and a submission without a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 will not avoid issuance. If an RCE complying with 1.114 is filed after issue fee payment and a petition under 1.313 is filed and granted, prosecution will be reopened but applicant may not obtain a refund of the issue fee. If application is subsequently allowed, the Notice of Allowance will reflect any difference in issue fee amounts due. Use Form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened after allowance or Quayle action.

rubrics_metrics.name: After appeal but before Board decision — withdrawal of appeal and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 after filing a Notice of Appeal to the Board but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper. The Office will withdraw the appeal upon filing of an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should advise the Board when an RCE is filed so the Board may vacate any decision rendered after the filing. If the RCE is proper (fee + submission responsive under 1.111), the finality of the last Office action will be withdrawn and submission entered. If not fully responsive but bona fide, use Form paragraph 7.42.08 to give applicant time to complete reply. If improper (missing fee/submission or non-bona fide), withdraw the appeal and treat the application under MPEP § 1215.01: if no claim allowed, application abandoned; if at least one allowed claim, pass to issue (use Form paragraphs 7.42.10–7.42.14 as applicable). Use Form paragraph 7.42.06 to notify applicant that the appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution reopened when RCE is proper.
